title: Manipur Spurious Liquor Death Toll Rises to 17, About 230 People in Hospital
excerpt: Sixteen of the dead are from Chandel district and one from Kakching. Officials say 1,130 people have been screened, six arrests made and 4,600 litres of illicit liquor seized.
body:
• The death toll in Manipur's suspected spurious liquor tragedy rose to 17 on Sunday, up from 11 reported on Friday, officials said.
  • Sixteen of the dead were from Chandel district and one from Kakching district; about 230 people remain admitted to hospitals and 38 are on dialysis.
  • Health teams have screened 1,130 people since the first death on the night of November 18.
  • Police have arrested six people and seized 4,600 litres of illicit liquor; a high-level inquiry headed by Principal Secretary R. K. Dinesh is to report within a month.

The death toll in the suspected spurious liquor tragedy in Manipur rose to 17 on Sunday, November 22, after one more person died, officials said. About 230 people are receiving treatment at hospitals across the state, in an update to the toll of 11 dead and 181 hospitalised that officials reported on Friday — our earlier report traced the first days of the incident in Chandel district.

Where the deaths occurred

A senior police official said 16 of the 17 deceased were from Chandel district and one was from Kakching district, according to PTI's report. The first death was that of Hrangbung Beruwang Anal, 50, of Nungpan village, on the night of November 18, followed by deaths in other villages over the next three days. Chandel District Superintendent of Police Dharmendra Kumar has reported that the liquor the victims consumed was reportedly purchased from Sugnu in neighbouring Kakching district.

The medical response

Health spokesperson Dr. Sapam Ranjan Singh said 1,130 people have been screened so far, of whom about 230 remain admitted, and 38 of them are undergoing dialysis. Treatment is being provided at the Regional Institute of Medical Sciences (RIMS), the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences (JNIMS) and several private hospitals, according to ReportWire's account of the official briefing. Doctors treating the patients suspect methanol poisoning, but officials have said the exact cause of the deaths has not yet been officially established and remains under investigation, pending laboratory tests.

Investigation and crackdown

Government spokesperson Thokchom Radheshyam Singh said samples of the suspected locally produced liquor have been sent to the National Food Laboratory in Kolkata, as well as to the Forensic Science Laboratory and the State Public Health Laboratory in Imphal. A high-level enquiry team headed by Principal Secretary R. K. Dinesh will submit its report to the government within a month. Raids on the sale of illegal liquor are continuing across the state; 4,600 litres of illicit liquor have been seized and six people arrested in connection with the incident, officials said.

"The government will not tolerate any activity that violates the law and strict action will be taken against offenders."

— Thokchom Radheshyam Singh, Manipur government spokesperson

What happens next

The laboratory results will determine what the victims actually consumed, and the Dinesh committee's report is due within a month. Screening continues, and health officials have urged anyone who drank locally brewed liquor of doubtful origin and develops symptoms — vomiting, abdominal pain, headache, dizziness, blurred vision or breathing difficulty — to seek medical care immediately rather than wait.
